newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Royal Dutch heads ADRs in NY.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Royal Dutch heads ADRs in NY.

text.p: Royal Dutch Petroleum Co rose in New York trade on Thursday to highlight the market in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Traders said ADRs were showing a bit more strength than the larger market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was off one to 6421 at midday.

"It's a little bit of nervous trading here," said Andrew Melinek, head of ADR sales and research at NatWest Securities. "The market is waiting and watching the Dow ... but it's shaken off the weakness of the last few days."

Royal Dutch rose 1-1/4 to 164-5/8 after Texaco Inc said a proposed refining-marketing alliance with Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc, a subsidiary of the Royal Dutch-Shell group, would go through in the first quarter of 1997.
The Netherlands' KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV rose one to 27-1/4 after the carrier said it would buy back $570 million in state-owned shares, cutting the government's stake to 25 from 38.2 percent.

British Gas Plc rose 3/8 to 36 following news of a new supply contract with British Petroleum . Enthusiasm was dampened, however, by concerns about dividend prospects once the company completed its planned demerger.
Israel's Teledata Communications Ltd was up 1-1/2 to 22-5/8 after Lehman Brothers raised its rating for the company to buy from outperform.
Advancers led decliners 244 to 221 among an 807-ADR index. Volume was 42.3 million shares.
